in game context ("I didn't think you'd do that!"), but as game design

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
OK, refresher: The RTR has said that Form of Mist (superior) can be
used to "continue" and action that was never blocked - like a Bum's Rush
for example.

"Continuing" this action has the effect of re-starting the action
resolution stage (actually, it backs up to even before this stage -
all the way to the Choose Blockers step, but that obvious bug isn't
the point of this post).

End refresher.

So, in the same vein, let's say the Acting Vampire *is* blocked,
resulting in combat. But, the poor acting vampire can't seem to draw
a FoM and so settles hand-to-claw combat, ending the combat quickly :-).

None too amused, the blocking vampire's Methuselah sends another
vampire into the fray with Fast Reaction (tapping the reacting
vampire, and starting a combat in the first round of which the acting
minion cannot strike). Somehow, the acting vampire lives through
the first round (probably playing a few damage prevention cards in
the process) and has the good fortune to draw a FoM.

The acting vampire presses, and the Fast Reactor starts turning a
little paler. The acting vampire chooses FoM superior for his strike
and continues the action at +1 stealth.

This is even further inside the bounds of the RTR's interpretation
of the way FoM works that the retro-booster effect on a Bum's Rush.

By reacting quickly, the vampire has unwittingly allowed a blocked
action to be successful when it would not have had the chance if
the fast reactor has sat on his thumbs.

I'd suggest allowing FoM to continue an action only if the acting

vampire is currently in combat with a blocking minion - to keep
silly stuff like the above from happening.

>Real world says no, card text and rules say yes (even if the FoM fix
>listed above is implemented). I'd say burn it, to avoid the mess involved
>with rules for obscure combinations of events.

Actually, I suspect the location is not burned in this case. If Vamp A's
action had been taken over by someone who didn't have a Bomb, the location
would not have been burned had the action been "successful." The principle
is that the result of a Masked action depends on what equipment the new
acting minion has, not what the old one had, and I see no particular reason
why this wouldn't or couldn't apply here. Similarly, if a vampire takes
a bleed action, what matters is whether it has a Laptop when the bleed is
successfull, not whether it had one when it took the action. If the vampire
gets into combat, loses the laptop, and Mists out of the combat, it will not
get that +1 bleed if the action is ultimately successfull.

But I will have to double check this with the others.
